title: Training & Fine-tuning
blurb: How a base model becomes a useful product. Pretraining at a glance, then the fine-tuning techniques that actually fit on a single engineer's GPU budget: SFT, instruction tuning, RLHF, DPO, LoRA, distillation.

nodes.label: The pretraining pipeline (overview)
nodes.description: Data, tokenization, mixed-precision training, optimizer state, checkpointing, the scale. You will not pretrain a frontier model — but you should understand the pipeline you're inheriting.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe the end-to-end pretraining pipeline at a level that lets you read a model card.

nodes.label: Data curation
nodes.description: Filtering, deduplication, quality scoring, mixing ratios, contamination. In 2026, data work is the highest-leverage thing most fine-tuners do.
nodes.doneWhen: You can design a small SFT dataset and defend each filtering and mixing choice.

nodes.label: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT)
nodes.description: Take a base model, train it on prompt-response pairs. The bread and butter of most adaptation work today.
nodes.doneWhen: You can run an SFT pass on a small open-weights model and evaluate the result.

nodes.label: Instruction tuning
nodes.description: SFT with instruction-following data, multi-task and multi-format. Why every base model needs this before it's product-shaped.
nodes.doneWhen: You can distinguish a base model from an instruction-tuned one by their outputs.

nodes.label: RLHF
nodes.description: Reward model + PPO, the InstructGPT recipe. Still the conceptual reference even where it's been replaced by simpler methods.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe the RLHF loop end-to-end and identify its three training stages.

nodes.label: DPO & direct preference methods
nodes.description: Direct Preference Optimization and the family of reward-model-free preference methods. The pragmatic default for preference learning in 2026.
nodes.doneWhen: You can explain why DPO simplified preference training versus RLHF and where it falls short.

nodes.label: LoRA / QLoRA / adapters
nodes.description: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning. Why you can fine-tune a 7B+ model on a single consumer GPU and why low-rank decomposition works.
nodes.doneWhen: You can fine-tune an open-weights model with LoRA on a single GPU and explain the rank/alpha trade-offs.

nodes.label: Distillation & model compression
nodes.description: Teacher-student training, distillation from a larger model into a smaller one, why this is the only practical path to cheap-fast specialized models.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe a distillation setup and identify when it's the right tool versus SFT.

nodes.label: Evaluation during training
nodes.description: Loss is not evaluation. Train-time evals: holdout sets, regression tests, mid-run sanity checks, the eval suite you need before you fine-tune anything serious.
nodes.doneWhen: You set up a meaningful eval suite before kicking off your first fine-tuning run, not after.

nodes.label: Distributed training infrastructure
nodes.description: Data parallel, tensor parallel, pipeline parallel, ZeRO / FSDP. How a frontier model trains across thousands of GPUs.
nodes.doneWhen: You can describe FSDP's sharding strategy and explain when tensor parallelism is required.
